f2_target.scope: generation-2 deterministic release ZIP repository component

predecessor_research.relationship: The earlier E1-E3 research established SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH / archive-normalization / variance-testing direction. This outcome does not repeat that work; it audits the newly implemented generation-2 builder against the resulting source boundary.

external_primary_or_authoritative_source.finding: Reproducibility means bit-for-bit identical specified artifacts given the same declared source, build environment and instructions.
Archive input ordering must be stable and must not inherit filesystem/locale ordering.
ZIP member timestamps can be normalized from a source-bound epoch rather than wall clock.
ZIP entries expose/serialize date_time, create_system, create_version, extract_version, flag_bits, internal_attr, external_attr, extra and comments; archive order is observable in infolist().
ZipInfo initializes create_version and extract_version from CPython DEFAULT_VERSION and serializes them; ZIP64 can append extra metadata even when caller-provided ZipInfo.extra starts empty.

observed_g2_strengths: member names are canonical POSIX relative paths and output members are sorted
source_date_epoch is explicitly normalized to ZIP's two-second timestamp resolution
create_system is fixed to POSIX and regular/executable modes are policy controlled
member/archive comments and caller extra fields are empty
payload bytes are hash/size rechecked after manifest construction
verifier checks sorted unique names, timestamp, create_system, compression, mode, comments/extra, canonical embedded manifest and payload hashes

remaining_architecture_gaps.observation: _zip_info() fixes create_system/compression/flag_bits/internal_attr/external_attr but leaves create_version and extract_version at ZipInfo runtime defaults even though those fields are serialized into ZIP headers.
remaining_architecture_gaps.counterhypothesis: Supported CPython versions may keep the same defaults forever, making the omission harmless in the supported environment.
remaining_architecture_gaps.falsifier: Build identical fixture under every supported interpreter/runtime; any archive SHA or raw central/local header difference attributable to version fields falsifies runtime-independent byte identity.
remaining_architecture_gaps.smallest_delta: Make serialized ZIP-version fields explicit policy or explicitly bind the supported builder runtime/version in the reproducibility perimeter; verifier should assert the selected values.

remaining_architecture_gaps.observation: builder opens ZipFile with allowZip64=True while verifier forbids any member extra metadata. CPython may generate ZIP64 extra records when size/count/offset thresholds require them, so a sufficiently large archive can conflict with the stated no-extra policy.
remaining_architecture_gaps.counterhypothesis: F2 release payload bounds may guarantee ZIP64 is unreachable.
remaining_architecture_gaps.falsifier: Prove a canonical maximum payload/member/count bound below ZIP64 thresholds, or construct a boundary fixture and show builder+verifier behavior.
remaining_architecture_gaps.smallest_delta: Choose one explicit v1 policy: (A) fail closed before ZIP64 and use allowZip64=False with documented bounds, preferred for the minimal release surface; or (B) admit and canonically verify only the exact required ZIP64 extra records. Do not leave builder acceptance broader than verifier acceptance.

remaining_architecture_gaps.observation: filename encoding/UTF-8 flag generation is performed by the zipfile runtime. Current canonical path validation permits non-ASCII names.
remaining_architecture_gaps.counterhypothesis: The supported path set may be ASCII-only or all supported runtimes may emit identical flags/bytes.
remaining_architecture_gaps.falsifier: Include at least one non-ASCII canonical path in a supported-runtime cross-host reproducibility fixture, or formally restrict v1 archive member names to a proven canonical encoding subset.
remaining_architecture_gaps.smallest_delta: Test first; restrict/bind only if the matrix falsifies byte identity.

recommended_trigger4_feed.implementation_shape: small fail-closed policy/test hardening inside existing WP1107 generation-2 lane; no new subsystem
acceptance: same bound fixture => identical archive SHA across declared supported builder environments
verifier accepts every archive the builder is allowed to produce
boundary that would require unadmitted ZIP64 fails before artifact handoff
serialized metadata fields covered by policy/verifier or by an explicit supported-runtime perimeter

explicit_nonclaims: No F2 target/VPS runtime was executed by this research outcome.
No whole-system, installation, physical GRID10, GWT/J-Space or completion credit is minted.
The identified gaps are source-level reproducibility risks until Trigger 4 reproduces/falsifies them in the owned implementation/test lane.
